page: Microsoft Azure D96pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpdsv6 server family. It is powered by a Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at 3.4 GHz, featuring 96 dedicated physical cores and 96 vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. The memory configuration consists of 384.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core. For local storage, the instance includes a bundled 5669 GB local disk and supports Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96pds_v6 demonstrates top-tier multi-core processing and memory subsystem performance. Multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core scores all rank in the top 10% of tested systems. The memory architecture delivers high throughput, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 10895.42 GB/sec and large block uncached write bandwidth at 205.46 GB/sec. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also achieve top-tier performance. Single-core performance, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, falls into the average tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D96pds_v6 offers high resource density by combining 96 dedicated ARM cores with a substantial 5669 GB local storage allocation, eliminating the need for separate storage attachments for data-heavy operations. The balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and strong multi-core performance make this server highly suitable for multi-threaded workloads, database hosting, Redis caching layers, software compilation, and static web serving.
